passages.text: Most adults can start exercising today. A small group should speak to a doctor first, and everyone should know the few signs that mean stop.

Should you see a doctor first?. Do you have chest pain, fainting, unusual breathlessness, a racing heartbeat or ankle swelling? · Stop here. See a doctor before exercising. · Go to the next question.. Has a doctor told you that you have heart, kidney or metabolic disease such as diabetes? · Get medical clearance first, then start light and build slowly. · Go to the next question.. Are you mostly inactive right now, exercising fewer than 3 days a week? · Start at light to moderate effort and build up over weeks. · Carry on, and build intensity gradually.. Screening rests on three things: how active you are now, any signs or known disease, and how hard you plan to train.

Normal during training. Muscles burning near the end of a set. Breathing hard, then recovering within a minute or two. Muscle soreness a day or two later. Stop and get help. Chest pain, pressure or tightness. Dizziness, faintness or confusion. A heartbeat that feels irregular or racing. Sharp or sudden joint pain
Some · activity is better than none, even if you cannot reach the target yet. Start low · and build slowly if you have been inactive
Pregnant, recovering from surgery, or managing a long-term condition? Follow your doctor's advice first. Levlofit will ask you and adjust.
Training is a signal. You stress the body a little more than it is used to, it recovers, and it rebuilds to handle that stress next time.
The adaptation loop. Train. Tire. Recover. Adapt. Do a little more

Four rules behind every plan. Specific · You get better at what you practise. Running builds running, lifting builds strength.. Progressive · Add a little over time: a rep, a set, a kilo or a minute.. Recovered · Levlofit tip: keep your rest days; they are part of the plan.. Consistent · Months of regular training beat any single perfect week.

Weekly aerobic activity for adults. Moderate, at least · 150 · 150 min [minutes a week]. Moderate, for more benefit · 300 · 300 min [minutes a week]. Or vigorous, at least · 75 · 75 min [minutes a week]. Or vigorous, for more benefit · 150 · 150 min [minutes a week]
2 · days a week · of muscle strengthening for all major muscles. Less · sitting · and more movement of any intensity in its place benefits health

The ACSM 2026 overview of 137 systematic reviews found that muscle growth did not depend on details such as load or how often you train, once weekly sets were equal. Its main advice: hard sets, at least twice a week, for all major muscles.
After a set, ask one question: how many more good reps could I have done? That number is your reps in reserve, or RIR.
Reps in reserve scale. 0 · Failure · No more reps possible with good form. 1 · Very hard · One rep left. 2 · Hard · Two reps left. 3 · Challenging · Three reps left. 4+ · Moderate · Four or more left
2 to 3 · RIR · is close enough to failure to build muscle. 30 to 100 · % of max · all build muscle when sets end near failure

Do. End most working sets with 1 to 3 reps left. Keep form identical on the last rep. Leave an extra rep in hand while learning a lift. Avoid. Taking every set to total failure. Grinding reps with form breaking down. Trusting your RIR guess in the first week of a new lift
Beginners are less accurate at judging reps in reserve than experienced lifters, and get better with practice. Start conservative.
A good warm-up raises body temperature, moves the joints you are about to use, and rehearses the first exercise with light weight.

A 10 minute warm-up. Raise · 3 to 5 minutes of easy movement: brisk walk, cycle or skipping.. Mobilise · Dynamic moves through full range: leg swings, arm circles, bodyweight squats.. Rehearse · 2 to 3 lighter sets of your first exercise, building up to your working weight.

Before hard training. Dynamic movements. Light sets of the main lift. Short static stretches if a sport needs the range. Save for later. Long static holds of 60 seconds or more per muscle. Stretching so hard it hurts
60 · seconds · or more of static stretching per muscle can reduce strength and power for a short time
Dynamic stretching has no negative effect and can help performance. Long static stretches cause a small, short-lived drop in force, so keep them after training.
Pick the goal, then match the dose. Strength wants heavy sets, muscle wants enough hard sets, and both want slow, steady progress.

Goal | Load | Volume | Frequency. Goal: Strength; Load: 80% of max or more; Volume: 2 to 3 sets per lift; Frequency: 2 or more sessions a week. Goal: Muscle size; Load: 30 to 100% of max, near failure; Volume: 10 or more sets per muscle a week; Frequency: Any, once weekly sets are reached. Goal: General health; Load: Any challenging load; Volume: All major muscles; Frequency: 2 or more days a week

Double progression, the simplest way to progress. Pick a rep range · For example 8 to 12 reps.. Add reps · Stay at the same weight until every set reaches the top of the range.. Add weight · Increase the load a little and drop back to the bottom of the range.. Repeat · Small steps, every week or two.
Example: 3 full-body days. Mon · Full body. Tue · Walk. Wed · Full body. Thu · Rest. Fri · Full body. Sat · Walk or sport. Sun · Rest
4 to 8 · weeks · between planned deloads is common practice. Less · volume and effort · during a deload week, to shed fatigue
Expert coaches agree a deload is a planned lighter period to shed fatigue and come back ready.
Build the plate first, then fix protein. Most Indian meals are rich in cereal and short on protein, so that is where training changes things.

My Plate for the Day, per 2000 kcal. Vegetables and greens · 400 · 400 g. Cereals and millets · 250 · 250 g. Fruits · 100 · 100 g. Pulses (30 g can be fish or meat) · 85 · 85 g. Nuts and seeds · 35 · 35 g. Oils and fats · 27 · 27 g. Milk or curd · 300 · 300 ml
Protein per kg of body weight, per day. Inactive adult, RDA · 0.8 · 0.8 g [g per kg]. Training adult, lower end · 1.4 · 1.4 g [g per kg]. Training adult, upper end · 2 · 2.0 g [g per kg]
20 to 40 · g · protein per meal, spread every 3 to 4 hours. 30 · % or less · of daily energy from fat. 0.83 · g per kg · is the Indian RDA for a healthy, inactive adult

Food, per 100 g raw | Protein | Energy. Food, per 100 g raw: Masoor dal; Protein: 24.4 g; Energy: 322 kcal. Food, per 100 g raw: Moong, whole; Protein: 22.5 g; Energy: 294 kcal. Food, per 100 g raw: Chicken breast, skinless; Protein: 21.8 g; Energy: 168 kcal. Food, per 100 g raw: Rajma, red; Protein: 19.9 g; Energy: 299 kcal. Food, per 100 g raw: Paneer; Protein: 18.9 g; Energy: 258 kcal. Food, per 100 g raw: Kala chana; Protein: 18.8 g; Energy: 287 kcal. Food, per 100 g raw: Egg, whole; Protein: 13.3 g; Energy: 135 kcal. Food, per 100 g raw: Atta; Protein: 10.6 g; Energy: 320 kcal. Food, per 100 g raw: Cow milk; Protein: 3.3 g; Energy: 73 kcal

Across 41 clinical studies, soy protein and isoflavones did not change testosterone or oestrogen in men, at any dose tested. Levlofit still caps soya chunks at 50 g dry a day, for variety rather than safety.
Start training well hydrated, and drink enough during long or hot sessions to avoid losing more than 2% of your body weight.
2 · % of body weight · lost as sweat is where performance starts to suffer

Check your sweat loss. Weigh before · Light clothes, after using the toilet.. Train · Note how much you drink.. Weigh after · Towel off first.. Compare · A 70 kg person should lose under 1.4 kg. More than that? Drink more next time.
Signs you are fine. Pale yellow urine. Signs to drink more. Dark urine, or very little of it. Headache or dizziness after training
Long sessions in heat lose salt as well as water. Salted food, lassi or chaas after training helps replace it.
Asian Indians carry more health risk at a lower weight than Western cut-offs assume, so Levlofit uses Indian cut-offs and your waist.
BMI for Asian Indians. 14 · 18 · Underweight [kg/m²]. 18 · 23 · Normal [kg/m²]. 23 · 25 · Overweight [kg/m²]. 25 · 35 · Obese [kg/m²]
Waist to height ratio. 0.3 · 0.5 · Healthy [ratio]. 0.5 · 0.6 · Increased risk [ratio]. 0.6 · 0.8 · High risk [ratio]

Measure your waist. Find the spot · Midway between your lowest rib and the top of your hip bone.. Breathe out · Relax, do not pull the belly in.. Read · Tape level and snug, not tight.. Divide · Waist in cm divided by height in cm.
BMI is good for. Quick screening. Tracking change in the same person. BMI misses. Muscle versus fat. Where fat is stored
You train in the gym and improve while you rest. Sleep is part of the plan, not time off from it.
7+ · hours · of sleep a night, regularly, for adults 18 to 60
Recovery in a week. Hard session. Easy day or rest. Sleep 7+ hours. Next hard session

Levlofit check-in: recovering well. Weights feel normal or lighter. You look forward to training. Sleep is steady. Levlofit check-in: too much fatigue. Performance drops for more than a week. Motivation keeps falling. Aches that do not settle
Hard and easy days. Mon · Hard. Tue · Easy walk. Wed · Hard. Thu · Rest. Fri · Hard. Sat · Easy. Sun · Rest
Coaches use planned lighter weeks, called deloads, to clear fatigue before it becomes a problem.
Food first. A few supplements have strong evidence and can help. None replaces training, sleep or enough protein from meals.

Supplement | Dose | Timing. Supplement: Creatine monohydrate; Dose: 3 to 5 g a day; Timing: Any time, every day. Supplement: Caffeine; Dose: 3 to 6 mg per kg; Timing: About 60 min before. Supplement: Protein powder; Dose: 20 to 40 g a serving; Timing: When meals fall short

3 to 5 · g a day · of creatine keeps muscle stores full, no loading needed. 0.3 · g per kg · a day for 5 to 7 days fills stores faster, if you choose to load. 3 to 6 · mg per kg · of caffeine improves performance, about 60 minutes before
Caffeine for a 70 kg person. Effective, low end (3 mg/kg) · 210 · 210 mg [mg]. Effective, high end (6 mg/kg) · 420 · 420 mg [mg]

Creatine has been studied for up to 5 years at 0.3 to 0.8 g per kg a day, in healthy people and in patients, with no adverse health risks found. Protein powder is simply protein: a serving counts the same as protein from food.

Worth it. Creatine monohydrate for strength and muscle. Caffeine for performance, if it suits you. Protein powder if food cannot reach your target. Be careful. Caffeine late in the day, it can cut sleep. Any supplement with a health condition: ask a doctor first
Wanting to get strong, run and look good all at once is normal. Training all of it from day one is how beginners stall.

Where do you start?. Can you squat, hinge, push and pull with good form? · Build your main goal first · Foundation phase first. Has your main goal reached Level 2? · Add a second goal · Keep building the main goal. Your level, not your wish list, decides how many goals you train.

How Levlofit levels you up. Check your level · Answer a short test for each goal based on what you can do today.. Foundation · Full-body basics and your main goal, 2 to 3 days a week.. Pass the check · Each level lists what to show before moving up.. Unlock the next goal · Extra goals switch on one at a time as your main goal climbs.
Stack goals when. Your main goal is past the basics. You recover well between sessions. Wait when. Form on basic lifts is not solid yet. Lots of running would compete with your strength work
More · interference · on strength and size from frequent, long running sessions
Combining endurance and strength training costs some strength, size and especially power gains, and the cost grows with how often and how long the endurance sessions are.
Rest long enough to repeat good reps. Cutting rest short saves minutes but costs quality.
Rest to aim for. Big lifts for strength · 2 · 2 min or more [minutes]. Muscle building · 1.5 · over 1 min [minutes]. Light accessory work · 1 · about 1 min [minutes]
2 · minutes or more · of rest maximises strength gains. 60 · seconds plus · may give a small edge for muscle growth; the evidence is uncertain
Using the rest timer. Tick the set · The timer starts on its own.. Breathe and reset · Sip water and think about the next set.. Go when ready · Skip early if you feel fresh, add time if not.
Strength improves with short rests too, but rests of 2 minutes or more give the most strength in both trained and untrained people.
Walking more is one of the simplest health wins, and you do not need 10,000 steps to get most of it.
Where the benefit levels off. Adults 60 and over · 7000 · 6,000 to 8,000 [steps a day]. Adults under 60 · 9000 · 8,000 to 10,000 [steps a day]
40 to 53 · % lower · risk of death in the most active step groups compared with the least
Add steps without trying. Walk after meals · Ten minutes after lunch and dinner adds up fast.. Take calls standing · Pace while you talk.. Stairs · Skip the lift for a few floors.
More daily steps went with lower risk, and the benefit levelled off at a lower count for older adults.
The scale moves with water, food and salt. Trends over weeks, the tape and photos together show what is really changing.

Tool | How often | Shows. Tool: Scale; How often: Daily or weekly, same time; Shows: Weight trend. Tool: Tape; How often: Every 2 to 4 weeks; Shows: Where size changes. Tool: Photos; How often: Every 4 weeks; Shows: Shape over months. Tool: Training log; How often: Every session; Shows: Strength going up
Make it consistent. Same time · Morning, after the toilet, before food.. Same conditions · Same light, pose and distance for photos.. Read the trend · Look at the line over weeks, not one reading.
Good signs. Waist down while strength goes up. Weight trend moving at the planned rate. Not a problem. Weight steady while the tape shrinks
Across 17 studies, regular self-weighing went with more weight loss and was not linked to anxiety or low mood.
Motivation comes and goes. Habits carry you on the days it does not show up.
66 · days · median time for a daily habit to feel automatic. 18 to 254 · days · the real range: some habits take far longer

Make a habit stick. Anchor it · Tie it to something you already do, like after brushing your teeth.. Start tiny · Two minutes of the habit beats a perfect plan you skip.. Track it · Tick it off in the Habits tab.. Miss once, not twice · One missed day barely affects the habit.
Daily water, from all drinks and food. Men · 2.5 · 2.5 L [litres]. Women · 2 · 2.0 L [litres]
Missing a single day did not meaningfully slow habit formation in the study.
Your weight trend follows energy balance: eat less than you burn and you lose, eat more and you gain. Levlofit estimates your burn, then sets food to match your goal.

How your calorie target is built. Resting burn (BMR) · The Mifflin-St Jeor equation: weight, height, age and sex give the energy you use at complete rest.. Activity · Levlofit multiplies BMR by 1.2 for a desk day up to 1.725 for a very active life, using your job or your training, whichever is higher. These multipliers are estimates, not measurements.. Goal · Fat loss eats about 15% below that, muscle gain about 10% above, everything else at maintenance.. Floor · Your target never goes below your BMR.
Mifflin-St Jeor | Formula, kcal a day. Mifflin-St Jeor: Men; Formula, kcal a day: 10 x kg + 6.25 x cm - 5 x age + 5. Mifflin-St Jeor: Women; Formula, kcal a day: 10 x kg + 6.25 x cm - 5 x age - 161

Activity multipliers Levlofit uses. Desk day, little walking · 1.2 · 1.2 [x BMR]. Light activity or 1 to 3 sessions · 1.375 · 1.375 [x BMR]. Active, 4 to 5 sessions · 1.55 · 1.55 [x BMR]. Very active, 6+ sessions or physical job · 1.725 · 1.725 [x BMR]
Why scale weight jumps day to day. Salt and carbs hold water. Water settles. The trend shows the truth
A moderate deficit preserves muscle and training quality better than a crash diet; maintenance with high protein suits beginners trying to lose fat and gain muscle together.
2 to 3 · weeks · of weight trend in Progress before you change calories: a Levlofit rule, because the formula is only an estimate
Fat loss is a slow, steady deficit with heavy training and high protein. Lose too fast and you lose muscle and strength with the fat.

Weekly weight loss. 0 · 0.5 · Slow and very safe [% of body weight]. 0.5 · 1 · Target pace [% of body weight]. 1 · 1.5 · Fast, muscle at risk [% of body weight]. 1.5 · 2.5 · Too fast [% of body weight]
0.5 to 1 · % a week · weight loss keeps the most muscle. 2.0 · g per kg · protein a day while dieting, the top of the ISSN minimum range; more may help when eating less

Keeps muscle. Lifting heavy 2 to 4 times a week. Protein at every meal. Losing about 0.35 to 0.7 kg a week if you weigh 70 kg. 7 or more hours of sleep. Costs muscle. Crash diets and skipped meals. Swapping lifting for only cardio. Dropping protein to save calories

Weight not moving?. Has the weekly average been flat for 3 weeks or more? · Go to the next question. · Levlofit rule: wait another week or two before changing anything.. Are you logging food honestly, including oil and snacks? · Levlofit rule: cut about 100 to 200 kcal a day, or add 2000 daily steps. · Track for one week first; most stalls are hidden intake.
Reviews of contest preparation find slower loss rates protect lean mass, and protein above normal needs helps most when lean and in a deficit.
Muscle is built slowly. A small surplus plus hard training adds muscle; a big surplus mostly adds fat.
Weekly weight gain, beginners and intermediates. 0 · 0.25 · Slow, lean [% of body weight]. 0.25 · 0.5 · Target pace [% of body weight]. 0.5 · 1 · Mostly fat [% of body weight]
10 to 20 · % surplus · above maintenance; Levlofit starts at 10%. 1.6 · g per kg · protein a day, where extra protein stops adding muscle on average

Eating more when you are never hungry. Add a meal · Milk and a banana, or curd and poha, between meals.. Use dense foods · Peanuts, a little ghee on roti, paneer, dry fruits.. Drink some calories · Milk, lassi or a banana shake.. Weigh weekly · Levlofit rule: if the trend is off pace for 3 weeks, adjust by 150 to 200 kcal a day.
In a meta-analysis of 49 trials, protein beyond about 1.6 g per kg a day gave no further average gain in muscle from training.

Lean gain. Small surplus, weight up slowly. Hard training 3 to 5 days a week. Advanced lifters: aim for the lower end. Dirty bulk. Eating everything in sight. Gaining over 1% a week. Long fat-loss diet needed afterwards
Carbs fuel training and fats keep hormones and cells healthy. Quality matters more than cutting either one out.
25 · g or more · naturally occurring fibre a day. 400 · g or more · vegetables and fruit a day. 40 to 70 · % of energy · from carbs fits a healthy diet when quality is good

Choose most days. Whole wheat atta, brown rice, millets like ragi, jowar and bajra. Dals, chana, rajma and sprouts. Whole fruit and plenty of vegetables. Nuts, seeds, mustard and groundnut oil. Limit. Maida, sugar, sweets and sugary drinks. Vanaspati (trans fats) and oil reused for frying. Lots of ghee, butter and coconut oil (saturated fat). Fried snacks most days
Upper limits for fat, share of daily energy. All fat · 30 · 30% or less [% of energy]. Saturated fat · 10 · 10% or less [% of energy]. Trans fat · 1 · 1% or less [% of energy]

Fibre in everyday food, per 100 g raw | Fibre. Fibre in everyday food, per 100 g raw: Kala chana; Fibre: 25.2 g. Fibre in everyday food, per 100 g raw: Whole moong; Fibre: 17.0 g. Fibre in everyday food, per 100 g raw: Rajma; Fibre: 16.6 g. Fibre in everyday food, per 100 g raw: Wheat atta; Fibre: 11.4 g. Fibre in everyday food, per 100 g raw: Ragi; Fibre: 11.2 g. Fibre in everyday food, per 100 g raw: Guava; Fibre: 8.6 g
Add fibre slowly over a week or two and drink water with it, so your gut can adjust.
You can build muscle on a vegetarian or vegan diet. It takes planning: protein-dense foods at every meal and a mix of sources.
51.5 · g protein · in 100 g of dry soya chunks, the richest common vegetarian source

Food, per 100 g raw | Protein | Energy. Food, per 100 g raw: Masoor dal; Protein: 24.4 g; Energy: 322 kcal. Food, per 100 g raw: Moong dal; Protein: 23.9 g; Energy: 326 kcal. Food, per 100 g raw: Peanuts; Protein: 23.7 g; Energy: 520 kcal. Food, per 100 g raw: Chana dal; Protein: 21.6 g; Energy: 329 kcal. Food, per 100 g raw: Paneer; Protein: 18.9 g; Energy: 258 kcal

A high-protein vegetarian day. Breakfast · Moong chilla or besan cheela, or poha with peanuts and curd.. Lunch · Dal plus rajma or chana with roti; pulses and grains cover each other's gaps.. Snack · Roasted chana, sprouts chaat or a glass of milk.. Dinner · Soya chunk curry, paneer bhurji or tofu with vegetables.
Soy did not change male hormones across clinical studies, at any dose tested.

Vegetarian staples. Paneer, curd and milk. Dals, chana and rajma. Soya chunks. Vegan staples. Tofu and soya chunks. Dals, chana, rajma and sprouts. Peanuts; aim for the upper end of your protein range
Total daily food matters most. Timing is fine-tuning: spread protein through the day and do not train on an empty tank.
